rows.note: This is the everyday Hong Kong Cantonese way to say that someone rides a bicycle.

example.english: We like to cycle on our days off.
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 fong3 gaa3 zung1 ji3 caai2 daan1 ce1

rows.note: This is the all-purpose everyday choice for the pedal-powered vehicle sense of “cycle.”

example.jyutping: ngo5 caai2 daan1 ce1 faan1 gung1

rows.note: Use this when something repeats or is put through a recurring cycle rather than when someone rides a bicycle.

example.english: The machine will cycle the water for reuse.
example.traditional: 部機會將啲水循環再用。
example.jyutping: bou6 gei1 wui5 zoeng1 di1 seoi2 ceon4 waan4 zoi3 jung6

rows.note: Use this for a process or sequence that returns to its starting point and repeats.

example.jyutping: ni1 go3 cing4 zeoi6 wui5 bat1 dyun6 ceon4 waan4

rows.note: Use this for the recurring interval itself, or in technical expressions such as a menstrual or electoral cycle.

example.english: This menstrual cycle is twenty-eight days.
example.traditional: 呢個月經周期係二十八日。
example.jyutping: ni1 go3 jyut6 ging1 zau1 kei4 hai6 ji6 sap6 baat3 jat6

rows.note: Use this for one complete turn or rotation, rather than for a recurring process.

example.english: The wheel stops after one cycle.
example.jyutping: go3 leon4 zyun2 jat1 zyun2 zau6 ting4 zo2
